LESSON: RADIOACTIVITY AND STABILITY OF ISOTOPES

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: PHYSICS
Strand: Waves and Optics
Topic 2.2: Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes, part of Waves and Optics in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 PHYSICS.

Key inquiry question: How is radioactivity important in day to day life? 2. What are the risks of exposure to radiation?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explain the terminologies used in radioactivity,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify the types and properties of radioactive emissions in nature,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. illustrate how radionuclides attain their stability using nuclear equations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. explain the terminologies used in radioactivity,

   Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. identify the types and properties of radioactive emissions in nature,

   Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. illustrate how radionuclides attain their stability using nuclear equations,

   Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Search and discuss with peers in groups the meaning of terms used in radioactivity (nuclear stability, radioactivity, half- life, nuclide, nucleotides, radioactive decay radioisotope, and background radiation). Learners with speech 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Search and discuss with peers in groups the meaning of terms used in radioactivity (nuclear stability, radioactivity, half- life, nuclide, nucleotides, radioactive decay radioisotope, and background radiation). Learners with speech 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: the learner practices how to organize their own learning by learning independently as they

construct a simple leaf electroscope using locally available materials.

● Self-efficacy: the learner develops the skill of effective communication by executing tasks while performing

experiments to verify the uses of an electroscope in electrostatics.

Values:
● Respect: the learner shows acceptance as they understand and appreciates others when searching, discussing in groups

and presenting findings on safety precautions when handling radioactive substances.

● Peace: the learner shows care by avoiding to hurt others while working with peers to demonstrate the detection of

radioactive emissions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Citizenship education: the learner practices peace and conflict resolution mechanisms as a way of promoting peace while

searching from print and non-print media, on applications of radioactivity.

● Socio-Economic and Environmental issues: the learner demonstrates environmental conservation awareness as they

search, discuss in groups and present findings on safety precautions when handling and disposing radioactive substances.

47

● Suggested Assessment Modes

● Oral /aural assessment.

● Observation.

● Written assessment.

● Peer assessment.

● Portfolio.

● Individual assessment.

● Experimentation

Suggested Learning Resources

Adapted digital media with assistive technology, print media in appropriate font and colour contrast, manilla papers, marker

pens, adapted writing materials, print graphs, leaf electroscope, photographic emulsion plate, cloud chamber, GM tube,

burette, digital talking stopwatch.
